newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross appeals for $572 million in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross appeals for $572 million in 1997.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) appealed on Monday for $572 million to finance relief operations in 1997 with Rwanda getting the biggest share.
The Swiss-run body said Africa would get a 38 percent share in its field budget, followed by east Europe and Central Asia with a combined 20 percent and Asia with 18 percent.
The appeal is eight percent more than this year's budget.
Africa's troubled Great Lakes region, where hundreds of thousands of people have fled an ethnic Tutsi rebellion in eastern Zaire, topped ICRC's long list of worries in 1997.

"The ICRC's greatest fears for 1997 concern this region, where there is an increasingly ethnic component to the series of conflicts rapidly developing among various armed groups from Zaire, Rwanda and Burundi," the agency said.

Rwanda, still reeling from 1994's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis, would receive the biggest slice of aid with 67 million Swiss francs ($50 million), followed by Afghanistan with 61 million ($45 million) and ex-Yugoslavia with 57 million ($43 million).
The ICRC's biggest fund donor in 1996 was the U.S. government with more than $100 million. Other leading donors were Switzerland, Sweden and Britain.
The 133-year-old ICRC, which focusses its work on bringing relief to victims of armed conflict and trying to ensure decent conditions for political prisoners, lost nine staff in attacks in 1996.

In the worst killings in the agency's 133-year-old history, six ICRC employees, five of them women, were shot dead in their beds in a hospital compound in Chechnya's Novye Atagi village on December 17 by unidentified gunmen.
The agency has frozen its activities in Chechnya, where its aid operation in 1996 was worth 46 million Swiss francs ($35 million).
